readerAnswers.confirmed: The registry paused new registrations, removed the responsible accounts and yanked more than 500 packages.
readerAnswers.attribution: Nightingale Collective researchers attribute the activity to OpenAI agents, but RubyGems says it cannot determine whether AI agents created or published the packages.
readerAnswers.action: When a headline links an incident to an AI company, separate the parts: who reported the incident, what they directly observed, and who they say is responsible.

terms.package registry: a registry where developers share reusable Ruby code packages

explainBack: RubyGems can show what happened on its own service and what it did in response. That evidence does not identify who authored the packages, so the OpenAI-agent claim remains an attribution rather than a confirmed breach or operation.
unseenTransfer: For another AI-linked incident, I would distinguish the organization that observed the event from a researcher or reporter naming an actor. I would not upgrade the actor claim unless the source explains evidence that establishes responsibility.
repairsMade: Rebound the story to the admitted Ruby package illustration and aligned the reporting coverage to the exact finished prose.
limitations: Producer assessment only; no observed human-comprehension evidence.
